records.document_title: Airworthiness — Technical Guidance Material and Type Acceptance information
records.verified_statement: The official SACAA Airworthiness page lists Engineering Unit TGM for Design Organisation Approval, Type Certification, Type Acceptance, Aircraft Flight Manual, Experimental Certificate of Airworthiness and Amateur-Built Aircraft, as well as Airworthiness guidance including Mass and Balance. The page states Type Acceptance is the authority's acceptance of a foreign type certificate with any additional limitations or conditions.
records.applicability: Primary authority source-discovery lead for AER-01. The applicable aircraft category, applicant route and certification basis remain pending direct SACAA Engineering confirmation.

records.document_title: CS-23 Amendment 6 and AMC & GM to CS-23 Issue 5 (ED Decision 2026/003/R)
records.verified_statement: EASA published CS-23 Amendment 6 and AMC/GM Issue 5 on 15 April 2026. EASA guidance states that the AMC/GM issue current on the application date is used as reflected in the certification programme, while prior or later issues may be agreed subject to the specific remarks and programme.
records.applicability: Comparator for a potential normal-category development pathway only. It is not a South African certification basis and cannot be treated as binding on SACAA without authority determination.

source.representation: Official EASA publication listing and Easy Access Rules webpage; source document bytes not yet pinned.

open_questions: Would CS-23 be the appropriate class/basis for either aircraft family?

records.claim_ceiling: EASA comparator baseline only; no certification-basis selection.

records.verified_statement: EASA's current Easy Access Rules state that it has not yet accepted ASTM F3239-22a as an AMC for CS-23 electric propulsion units. EASA says it would consider an applicant using the standard as a basis for proposed means of compliance subject to agreement.
records.applicability: Do not label F3239-22a as an EASA-accepted AMC. It may be considered as a proposed basis only after authority agreement. SACAA position is unknown.

records.document_title: ASTM F3316-19 — Electrical Systems for Aircraft with Electric or Hybrid-Electric Propulsion
records.verified_statement: EASA's Easy Access Rules include a remark that EASA has not yet accepted ASTM F3316-19 for electrical systems installed on aeroplanes with electric or hybrid-electric propulsion, while indicating that an applicant's proposed use may be considered subject to agreement.
records.applicability: Do not treat F3316-19 as an accepted EASA AMC. Treat as candidate material only if an authority agrees to the proposed means. SACAA position unknown.

source.representation: Official EASA Easy Access Rules webpage; current status of any subsequent revisions not separately established.

open_questions: Has a later revision or alternate EASA means been accepted since this issue?

records.claim_ceiling: Specific EASA remark recorded as of the retrieved Issue 5 page; must be rechecked at programme baseline.

records.authority: ASTM International (standard publisher); EASA references F2490-20 in AMC material
records.jurisdiction: International / US industry comparator; EASA comparator
records.document_title: ASTM F2490-20 — Standard Guide for Aircraft Electrical Load and Power Source Capacity Analysis
records.verified_statement: ASTM describes F2490-20 as an aircraft-level electrical load analysis guide covering source/converter/bus capacity and average/maximum demands under probable load combinations and durations. Its published scope explicitly states that electric propulsive-power load analysis was not considered in its development.
aer01_relevance: Maintenance of electrical load analysis after aircraft changes
records.applicability: Useful for the non-propulsive aircraft electrical load-analysis discipline; not sufficient by itself for traction motor, inverter, battery, generator and propulsion bus sizing for a hybrid-electric aircraft.

source.representation: Official ASTM standard catalogue/scope page; full standard is licensed.

open_questions: What additional electric-propulsion load-analysis method and accepted means should cover propulsion power and source transients?
How will load-analysis evidence be maintained after configuration, equipment and software changes?
records.claim_ceiling: Scope limitation verified; no claim that F2490-20 is an electric-propulsion compliance method.
